modern: From Sextus, a kindly disposition, and the example of a household governed in a fatherly way, and the idea of living in keeping with nature; and dignity without affectation, and to look carefully after the interests of friends, and to put up with ignorant people, and those who form opinions without thinking: he had the ability to adapt himself readily to everyone, so that conversation with him was more pleasant than any flattery; and at the same time he was most highly respected by those who spent time with him: and he had the ability both to discover and to arrange, in an intelligent and methodical way, the principles necessary for life; and he never showed anger or any other passion, but was entirely free from passion, and also most affectionate; and he could express approval without noisy display, and he had much knowledge without showing it off.
original: From Sextus, a benevolent disposition, and the example of a family governed in a fatherly manner, and the idea of living conformably to nature; and gravity without affectation, and to look carefully after the interests of friends, and to tolerate ignorant persons, and those who form opinions without consideration: he had the power of readily accommodating himself to all, so that intercourse with him was more agreeable than any flattery; and at the same time he was most highly venerated by those who associated with him: and he had the faculty both of discovery and ordering, in an intelligent and methodical way, the principles necessary for life; and he never showed anger or any other passion, but was entirely free from passion, and also most affectionate; and he could express approbation without noisy display, and he possessed much knowledge without ostentation.

explained.summary:
Sextus, a philosopher Marcus studied with, combined warmth with dignity. He ran his household like a kind father, lived in line with nature, looked after his friends’ interests and was patient with people who hadn’t thought things through. He fitted in with anyone, so that talking to him felt better than being flattered, yet everyone respected him.

He was calm without being cold, and knew a great deal without showing it off. Marcus admires the balance: easy company, but serious underneath.
explained.today: Picture the colleague everyone likes talking to, who listens to the person with half-baked opinions without rolling their eyes and praises good work without making a big show of it, yet is quietly the most knowledgeable person in the room.
